The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 19.02.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 19.02.2024 at about 6.45 p.m., the petitioner was riding the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-54-M-0454 on Chikkade Circle, Pandavapura - Mandya main road, Pandavapura Taluk, Mandya, at that time, the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-11-EW-3013 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed SCCH-10 against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the injured petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, Pandavapura and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Kennalu hospital, Mysuru, wherein he took inpatient treatment from 19.02.2024 to 01.03.2024.
Later on, the petitioner again admitted to said Kennalu hospital on 05.03.2024 to 08.03.2024.
He has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, he was owner cum lorry driver and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EW-3013.
The respondent No.1 being owner and respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the SCCH-10 present claim petition.
3. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

4. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 being the insurer contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable.
Further contended that the vehicle in question Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EW-3013 was covered by Bundled policy and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.2 has denied the accident,
the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.

Further denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation SCCH-10 and income of the petitioner.
Further contended that, the petitioner himself was solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 19.02.2024 at about 6.45 p.m., while he was proceeding in a Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-54-M-0454 on Chikkade Circle, Pandavapura, Mandya Main Road, at that time, the rider of the Pulsar Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EW-3013 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, as a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
SCCH-10 6.
The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW-2 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :

9. ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 19.02.2024.
To substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW2 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.
Ex .P.1 SCCH-10 is the copy of the FIR No.0037/2024 of Pandavarura PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O.
has registered a case against the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11- EW-3013 for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Pandavarapura PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.6, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr.
Vinoda. M, who is none other than the rider of offending Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No. KA-11-EW-3013 for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

10. Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.9 produced by petitioner and Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.8 discharge summaries, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

11. On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending SCCH-10 vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

12. The respondent No.2 have seriously disputed the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and contended that, the petitioner himself solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident as he was riding the same in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the moving vehicle.

Though the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the petitioner and there is no negligent act on the part of the rider of the offending Motor cycle, they have not produced any contra documents to show that, the petitioner has also contributed to the accident.
Further the police have not registered any case against the petitioner for his alleged negligent act.

13. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending Motor cycle showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the SCCH-10 police records, it reveal that the rider of the offending vehicle was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
14. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EW-3013.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
SCCH-10 16. ISSUE No.2:-

As stated above, the petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of rider of offending Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA- 11-EW-3013.
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

He further stated that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government hospital, Pandavapura and after first aid treatment he was shifted to Kennalu hospital, Mysuru wherein he took inpatient treatment from 19.02.2024 to 01.03.2024 and again from 05.03.2024 to 08.03.2024.
17.

Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for SCCH-10 convenience.

Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising):
 Loss of earning during the period of
treatment

; 
b. Loss of future earning on account of permanent disability.
Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

sentences.text: Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire SCCH-10 materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.9.

As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained, 1) fracture right distal end radius,
proximal phalanx middle finger right hand and 3) Crush injury to right foot.
18. In this case, the petitioner has produced two discharge summaries of Kennalu hospital as per Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.8.
On perusal of Ex.P.7 it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital on 19.02.2024 and discharged on 01.03.2024.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8, it reveals that again the petitioner admitted to the said hospital on 05.03.2024 and discharged on 08.03.2024.
19.
Ex.P.13 are the medical bills (20 in Nos.) amounting to Rs.3,06,594/- and Ex
.P.14 are the medical prescriptions.
I have carefully perused the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
Out of the said medical bills, Sl.No.1 and Sl.No.4 are the final bills.
The amount in Sl.No.2 is already included in Sl.No.1 final bill.
The amount in Sl.No.5 and Sl.No.6 are SCCH-10 already included in Sl.No.4 final bill.
Sl .No.8 and Sl.No.9 are the advance receipts of Rs.40,000/- and Rs.32,000/-.
Therefore, the medical bills i.e. Sl.No.2, 5, 6 8 and 9 are not taken for consideration.
After deducting the said bills, the total medical bills amount would be Rs.2,18,980/-.
The said medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for medial bills of Rs.2,18,980/- and same is rounded off to Rs.2,19,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
20. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
21. The petitioner has contended that, before the accident SCCH-10 he was hale and healthy and he was owner cum lorry driver by profession and earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to the injuries he is not able to do any work as he was doing earlier and also lost his income.
22. On behalf of the petitioner, the Doctor was examined as PW-2.

PW-2 in his evidence has deposed that, injured petitioner has sustained fractures and he under went surgery of open reduction internal fixation with plate and screws for right distal end radius fracture, wiring and wound debridement + K-wiring and disarticulation of right 4th toe with wound debridement.
PW-2 doctor has assessed physical disability of the both limb at 50.4% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 25%.
Though the PW-2 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
23. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 53 years SCCH-10 at the time of accident and he was owner cum lorry driver and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.10, driving licence as per Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 10.01.1971.
The accident was occurred on 19.02.2024.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 53 years at the time of accident for multiplier.

sentences.text: Further, to prove the occupation and income of the petitioner, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

entities.text: Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the SCCH-10 notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/- Hence, the notional income has to be considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 19-02-2024.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
25. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
26. As per the doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 25%.
It is settled principles that all SCCH-10 permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 25% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 20%.
27.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 53 years.
Hence, 9 multiplier is applicable.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 20%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,98,000/-(Rs.16,500 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income will be Rs.1,98,000/-(annual income) X 11 (multiplier) X 20% = Rs.4,35,600/-.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.4,35,600/-.

28. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today SCCH-10 activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.

Hence, I conclude that if Rs.25,000/-
is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.
doctor in his evidence has stated that, petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.

But during the cross-examination,
he has stated that, in their hospital the expenses will be around Rs.20,000/-.
Admittedly, the petitioner has not produced any estimation for removal of implants.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, if Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses it will be just and this amount shall not carry any future interest.

Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
SCCH-10 Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
 1) Medical expenses Rs. 2,19,000 /-
 2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-
 3) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 15,000 /-
 Loss of Future earning Rs. 4,35,600/-
 4) capacity due to permanent  disability  5) Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000 /-
 6) Future Medical expenses Rs. 20,000/-
 Total Rs.7,44,600/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,44,600/-.
31. REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-11-EW-3013.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.

Therefore, this Court is SCCH-10 of the opinion that,
the respondent No.1 being RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 being insurer are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation of Rs.7,44,600/- along with interest @
6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,44,600/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The SCCH-10 respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 30% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E- payment on proper identification.
